details:
Currently the performance ranking system has some major inaccuracy problems with things being skewed in such a way that a 70001 poly 1 material single skinned mesh with no shape keys and no physbones is very poor, however 70000 polys with hundreds of shape keys, 32 material slots, 16 skinned meshes, 256 phys bone transforms, and thousands of particles with hyper complex particles and a single very high resolution shadow casting point light and 32 seperate animators is somehow better.

I think some statistics need to be looked at

1: Poly count, I'd suggest seperating polygons, skinned polygons, and blendshape polygons in terms of ranking, I would also make the limits graunlar like how they are on the quest version so that there's a reason to go for a polycount other than literally just under the very poor cutoff (name a popular PC avatar that isn't just 69999 polys that isn't very poor due to polycount), I also think the limit should be adjusted since very poor is supposed to be the "I can't optimize to save my life" rank, some examples I can think of for PC are

Excellent: 15000 Blendshape polys, 32000 Skinned polys, 48000 Polys

Good: 32000 Blendshape Polys, 70000 Skinned Polys, 100000 Polys

Medium: 50000 Blendshape Polys, 80000 Skinned Polys, 125000 Polys

Poor: 70000 Blendshape Polys, 150000 Skinned Polys, 250000 Polys (Honestly I'd do some stress testing with all 3 types of polys with different graphics cards to figure out the ratios to go by)

2: Cloth, performance with the cloth component has improved significantly since the performance rank system was added, maybe increase the limits based on stress testing in the current unity version.

3: lights, personally I think there should be a distinction between the guy using a non-important light without shadows that only casts onto his own avatar, and the guy with a very high resolution shadow casting per pixel point light, I would have a distinction for people using directional lights on an unused layer to force the depth buffer to be shown, but honestly I'd rather just have a more performant native solution to getting the depth buffer without having to put lights on our avatars than to encourage it.

4: Bounds size, how exactly does this affect performance on its own?

5: Shaders, if it's possible, maybe penalize using shell rendering (the thing that makes a lot of fur shaders really really laggy) or tesselation, or other really expensive shader operations by having that factor into the performance rank.

6: Animator Layers, these are notorious for causing serious framerate problems and can easily be optimized by using direct trees instead, maybe encouraging this optimization would be a good idea (if exceeded by MDPR, replace animation layers with stock VRchat animations)

7: Mesh VRAM usage, speaks for itself.

PS: I'd also look into solutions to some Minimum Displayed Performance Rank woes solutions, such as displaying a lower mip level if available on avatars that are very poor due to texture memory usage.
title: Revise Performance Ranking System
